subject: Clarify multi-region commit tiers & per-token billing (US/EU/APAC)
messages:
From: Elena Morris <elena.morris@atlashealth.ai>
To: Sean Gallagher <sean_gallagher@redwood.com>
Cc: procurement@atlashealth.ai
Date: 2026-04-01T09:12:00-07:00
Subject: Question on commit tiers across regions

Hi Sean,

Thanks again for the demo last week — the latency numbers looked promising. Before we move to a formal commitment, procurement asked for a clarification on how Redwood applies committed spend and per-token discounts across regions. A few concrete questions: 

- If we sign a single 12-month committed spend (USD) at X tokens/month, does that commit pool apply globally (US/EU/APAC) or is it split by region for billing and discounting?
- Are region-specific price multipliers applied on top of the per-token price (we noticed higher list prices for APAC in the brochure)?
- How does overage work if we exceed the monthly commit in one region but are under in another — is it netted?
- For compliance reasons, some EU traffic must remain in EU-only private deployments. Can we get the same commit discounts for traffic served from private EU capacity?

I've attached a small rollup of our Q1 usage by region to help contextualize. Procurement hopes to have a rulebook so finance can model FY27.

Best,
Elena
Procurement Lead, Atlas Health

Attachments: Atlas_Rollup_Usage_Jan-Mar.csv (CSV, 43 KB)

From: Sean Gallagher <sean_gallagher@redwood.com>
To: Elena Morris <elena.morris@atlashealth.ai>
Cc: Laura Bennett <laura_bennett@redwood.com>, Marissa Cole <marissa_cole@redwood.com>
Date: 2026-04-02T11:05:00-07:00
Subject: Re: Question on commit tiers across regions

Hi Elena — thanks for the clear data; that helps a lot. Quick answers up-front, then I'll follow with a short summary of options we can put in the SOW: 

- Commit scope: by default, a single account-level committed spend is global and applied across regions (we net usage against the commit). That means if you underuse in EU but overuse in US, the overage is charged at the agreed per-token overage rate, but the total monthly usage is evaluated against the global commit first.
- Region price multipliers: list prices can differ by region due to local infra costs and taxes. For committed tiers we typically surface a single blended per-token price (USD) that applies to netted global usage. However, customers sometimes request a regional carve-out for legal/residency reasons — see below.
- Overage handling: we net monthly usage across regions against the global commit. Overage tokens beyond the committed volume are billed at the overage per-token rate (or the next tier if you cross into it). We can also offer smoothing (see billing rules option #2).
- Private/EU carve-outs: you can keep EU traffic on private capacity. We can offer commit crediting against private usage, but it requires the private deployment to be included in the same billing account and a short addendum to the MSA to confirm data residency and billing mapping.

I'm looping in Laura (pricing/sales ops) and Marissa (enterprise AE) to propose two practical packaging options for your finance team. I'll also attach a draft clause for the SOW on billing mapping.

Next: would 30 minutes tomorrow or Friday work for a quick call to run models with your Q1 rollup?

Thanks,
Sean
Senior Account Executive, Redwood Inference

Attachments: Draft_MSA_Atlas-Redwood_v1.pdf (PDF, 128 KB)

From: Laura Bennett <laura_bennett@redwood.com>
To: Sean Gallagher <sean_gallagher@redwood.com>, Elena Morris <elena.morris@atlashealth.ai>
Cc: Marissa Cole <marissa_cole@redwood.com>
Date: 2026-04-03T08:22:00-07:00
Subject: Re: Question on commit tiers across regions

Hi all — jumping in with 2 standard packaging options (we can tailor):

Option A — Global Net Commit (recommended for multi-region customers)
- Single committed token pool (USD) across all regions.
- Blended committed per-token price quoted in USD.
- Overage billed monthly at the contracted overage rate.
- Netting: monthly usage is netted globally; no per-region carry.
- Benefit: simplest for finance modeling and typically yields the best blended price.

Option B — Regional Commit with Cross-Region Buffer
- Commit expressed as regional allocations (US/EU/APAC) with a small global buffer (e.g., 10% of total commit) that can be used in any region.
- Regional list multipliers apply to the list price but discount is applied to the allocated regional pool.
- Overage in a region pulls from the global buffer first, then billed as overage.
- Benefit: helpful when legal/regulatory constraints require clear regional spend reporting.

Notes on Private/EU usage:
- Private EU deployments can be included in either option but must be on a single invoicing account.
- For strict data-residency (air-gapped) installs we have a separate Private license and discounts are typically treated as an enterprise add-on (not standard hosted commit).

I'll prepare a short modeling sheet that shows effective blended rates under both options given the Q1 numbers. Sean — happy to take call windows tomorrow 09:00-11:00 or Friday 13:00-16:00 PT.

Laura
Pricing Operations, Redwood Inference

From: Elena Morris <elena.morris@atlashealth.ai>
To: Sean Gallagher <sean_gallagher@redwood.com>
Cc: procurement@atlashealth.ai
Date: 2026-04-06T14:40:00-07:00
Subject: Re: Question on commit tiers across regions

Sean/Laura — thanks, that framing is helpful. A couple of clarifying follow ups from finance: 

1) If we go with Option A (Global Net Commit), can you guarantee that tax/duties and region-specific surcharges will not cause an effective USD-per-token divergence in our invoices? Finance is nervous about having to reconcile region-level taxes into the per-token metric they forecast.

2) For Option B, what does the 10% buffer look like in the contract? Is it a floating bucket that resets monthly?

3) We also want to understand the mechanics for a planned APAC pilot. It will be small to start (<=5% of total tokens). If the APAC pilot unexpectedly spikes, will it consume the global commit immediately or be subject to APAC list multipliers before netting?

Would appreciate a short note we can hand to accounting — the sooner we can get a one-page summary the better.

Best,
Elena

On attachments: the procurement team added a redline to the Draft MSA and asked for an explicit billing mapping exhibit. I can share that after we confirm approach.

From: Sean Gallagher <sean_gallagher@redwood.com>
To: Elena Morris <elena.morris@atlashealth.ai>
Cc: Laura Bennett <laura_bennett@redwood.com>, Marissa Cole <marissa_cole@redwood.com>
Date: 2026-04-08T09:10:00-07:00
Subject: Re: Question on commit tiers across regions

Elena — good questions. Short answers for accounting to hand to finance (I'll also attach a one-page summary after this):

1) Taxes and surcharges: we invoice in USD and show region-level taxes where required as separate line items. The contracted blended per-token price is exclusive of taxes and surcharges; taxes will not change the committed discounting mechanics but will appear on the invoice as separate tax lines. If you need a fully tax-inclusive committed price for forecasting, we can produce an illustrative model but final taxes will match local regulations.

2) Buffer mechanics for Option B: the buffer is a monthly floating bucket equal to 10% of the total committed tokens. It resets each billing period (calendar month). Usage first consumes regional allocation, then the buffer, then overage. We can change the buffer size if you want (5–20%).

3) APAC pilot behavior: usage is netted against the global commit. However, if you run private APAC capacity under a separate billing account or dedicated contract, that usage will not net unless we map it into the same invoicing account (we can do that with an exhibit). For hosted API traffic in APAC under the same account, it will consume the global commit immediately; list multipliers are only used when we quote list pricing for non-committed (on-demand) flows.

Action items: Laura will send a one-page "How commit billing works" and a modeled example using your Q1 numbers. Marissa — can you prepare a carve-out clause for Private EU so Elena has language procurement can redline?

Sean

From: Marissa Cole <marissa_cole@redwood.com>
To: Elena Morris <elena.morris@atlashealth.ai>, Sean Gallagher <sean_gallagher@redwood.com>
Cc: Laura Bennett <laura_bennett@redwood.com>
Date: 2026-04-12T15:04:00-07:00
Subject: Re: Question on commit tiers across regions

Elena — attaching the one-pager and a suggested Display Billing Exhibit for the SOW. Key excerpts below for quick review: 

- Global Net Commit: Customer commits to N tokens/month at USD X/token. Monthly invoice applies usage against the global pool. Taxes and local surcharges are itemized and do not affect the token netting.
- Regional Allocation Option: Customer may request allocated tokens per region. A monthly global buffer (default 10%) exists and resets every billing period.
- Private Deployment: EU private deployments may be included in the billing account if the customer provides the required account mapping; discounts for Private are applied as an enterprise addendum.

If that all looks OK I can fold these clauses into the Draft_MSA_Atlas-Redwood_v1.pdf and send a follow-up for signature.

Thanks,
Marissa
Enterprise AE, Redwood Inference
